You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Sign error: down shift should push bot to Hh-1, i.e., +(Hh-1-bot), not -(Hh-1-bot).
def solve(g):
    Hh,Ww=len(g),len(g[0])
    o=objs_of(g)
    out=[[0]*Ww for _ in range(Hh)]
    for c in o:
        xs=[x for y,x in c]
        up = sum(xs)/len(xs) < Ww/2
        top=min(y for y,x in c); bot=max(y for y,x in c)
        sh = -top if up else (Hh-1-bot)
        for y,x in c: out[y+sh][x]=g[y][x]
    return out

    Hh,Ww=len(g),len(g[0])
    o=objs_of(g)
    out=[[0]*Ww for _ in range(Hh)]
    for c in sorted(o,key=lambda c:(-len(c), sum(x for y,x in c)/len(c))):
        col=g[c[0][0]][c[0][1]]
        ys=[y for y,x in c]
        if min(ys)<=Hh-1-max(ys): step=-1
        else: step=1
        # start just beyond edge target? Place at initial position into out first? No—slide from edge.
        # Simulate: move object stepwise until next position would be invalid or occupied; then stop with LAST valid position.
        cur=c[:]
        placed=False
        while True:
            nxt={(y+step,x) for y,x in cur}
            if any(not(0<=y<Hh) or not(0<=x<Ww) or out[y][x]!=0 for y,x in nxt):
                break
            for y,x in nxt: out[y][x]=col
            cur=nxt
    return out

from collections import defaultdict as dd
def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    ci=comps(g)
    def sig(c):
        ys=[y for y,x in c]; xs=[x for y,x in c]
        return tuple(sorted((y-min(ys),x-min(xs)) for y,x in c)), min(ys), min(xs)
    pairs=dd(list)
    for c in ci:
        pairs[sig(c)].append(c)
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    occ=set()
    for sig_,mem in pairs.items():
        if len(mem)==1:
            c=mem[0]
            for y,x in c: out[y][x]=g[c[0][0]][c[0][1]]
            continue
        a,b=mem[0],mem[1]
        cols=g[a[0][0]][a[0][1]],g[b[0][0]][b[0][1]]
        ya,xa=sig(a)[1],sig(a)[2]; yb,xb=sig(b)[1],sig(b)[2]
        # top one (smaller start row) moves to bottom; bottom one moves to top
        ta,tb = (a,b) if ya<yb else (b,a)
        tcol, bcol = g[ta[0][0]][ta[0][1]], g[tb[0][0]][tb[0][1]]
        cbs=tuple((y,x) for y,x in tb); tas=tuple((y,x) for y,x in ta)
        # bottom member slides down until blocked by bottom edge or occupied cell
        cur=list(cbs)
        while True:
            nxt=[(y+1,x) for y,x in cur]
            if all(y<H and 0<=x<W and out[y][x]==0 and (y,x) not in occ for y,x in nxt):
                occ-=set(cur); occ|=set(nxt); cur=nxt
            else: break
        for y,x in cur: out[y][x]=tcol
        # top member slides up similarly
        cur=list(tas)
        while True:
            nxt=[(y-1,x) for y,x in cur]
            if all(y>=0 and 0<=x<W and out[y][x]==0 and (y,x) not in occ for y,x in nxt):
                occ-=set(cur); occ|=set(nxt); cur=nxt
            else: break
        for y,x in cur: out[y][x]=bcol
    return out
for nm in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    print(nm, f(G[nm+' input'])==G[nm+' output'])

def solve_model(g, mode='attr'):

    ci=comps(g)

    for c in ci:
        ys=[y for y,x in c]; xs=[x for y,x in c]

    # distance to nearest edge: min(min_row, H-1-max_row) etc.
    def dist2edge(y0,y1,H): return min(y0, H-1-y1)
    info.sort(key=lambda t:(dist2edge(t[0],t[1],H), t[0]))
    occ=set()
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for y0,y1,col,cells in info:
        h=y1-y0+1
        # direction: toward nearer edge

        cur=[list(c) for c in cells]
        if d==-1:
            while True:
                nxt=[(y-1,x) for y,x in cur]
                if all(y>=0 and (y,x) not in occ for y,x in nxt):

        elif d==1:

# Check overlap-adjacency model on demos 2 and 3: slide until blocked by overlap OR adjacency to occupied.
def solve(gi):
    gi=np.array(gi); H,W=gi.shape
    cs=comps(gi)
    n=len(cs)//2
    top=[c for c in sorted(cs,key=lambda c:-len(c[1]))[:n]]
    bot=[c for c in sorted(cs,key=lambda c:-len(c[1]))][n:]
    def anchored(cells,d):
        step=-1 if d=='up' else 1
        pos=list(map(tuple,cells))
        while True:
            nxt=[(y+step,x) for y,x in pos]
            if any(not(0<=y<H) for y,x in nxt): break
            adj=False
            for y,x in nxt:
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                    if (ny,nx) in occ and (ny,nx) not in nxt: adj=True
            if adj or any((y,x) in occ for y,x in nxt): break
            pos=nxt; occ.update(pos)
        return pos
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]; occ=set()
    for col,cc in top:
        p=anchored(cc,'up'); occ|=set(p)
        for y,x in p: out[y][x]=col
    for col,cc in bot:
        p=anchored(cc,'down'); occ|=set(p)
        for y,x in p: out[y][x]=col
    return out
for nm in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    print(nm, solve(G[nm+' input'])==G[nm+' output'])
